CHAPTER 2.2 · LEARNING AREA 2 · NOVEMBER · DECEMBER

Calculating with rational numbers

What is $-3 - 5$? And why does minus times minus give plus? In this chapter you calculate with all rational numbers: adding, subtracting, multiplying, dividing, raising to powers and taking roots. You do not have to take the rules on trust. You see on the number line and in number patterns why they hold.

16 LESSONS4 UNITS3 LABS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • add and subtract rational numbers
  • apply and justify the sign rules for multiplying and dividing
  • use the laws of arithmetic and the order of operations to calculate cleverly
  • decide: in your head, on paper or with a calculator
  • calculate powers with a negative base and take square roots

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Adding and subtracting

With the account: $30 - 45 = -15$, then $-15 + 20 = 5$, then $5 - 12 = -7$. The balance is $-€7$. On the number line, adding a positive number means: go to the right. Adding a negative number means: go to the left.

And how do you subtract a negative number? If someone takes away €5 of debt from you, you have €5 more. So subtracting a negative number means going to the right.

KEY POINT · ADDING AND SUBTRACTING

Subtracting means adding the opposite number: $\;a - b = a + (-b)$. So $\;7 - (-2) = 7 + 2 = 9\;$ and $\;3 + (-5) = 3 - 5 = -2$.

Same signs: add the absolute values; the sign stays. $\;(-4) + (-3) = -7$

Different signs: subtract the smaller absolute value from the bigger one and take the sign of the number with the bigger absolute value. $\;(-7) + 3 = -4$

Two minus signs next to each other are not written. You use brackets: $5 - (-3)$, not $5 - -3$.

In short: $+(-) \to -$ and $-(-) \to +$.

INTERACTIVE · CALCULATING ON THE NUMBER LINE
EXAMPLE 1 · WITH DECIMALS

Calculate $-2.5 - (-4)$ and $1.2 - 3.5$.

$-2.5 - (-4) = -2.5 + 4 = 1.5$

$1.2 - 3.5$: different signs, $3.5 - 1.2 = 2.3$. $1.2 - 3.5 = -2.3$

EXAMPLE 2 · WITH FRACTIONS

Calculate $-\tfrac12 + \tfrac13$.

Use a common denominator: $-\tfrac36 + \tfrac26$. The absolute value $\tfrac36$ is bigger, so the result is negative.

$-\tfrac12 + \tfrac13 = -\tfrac16$

In the morning it is −4 °C. By midday the temperature rises by 9 degrees, by the evening it falls by 7 degrees. Write down a calculation. How warm is it in the evening?

$-4 + 9 - 7 = -2$. In the evening it is −2 °C.

An account stands at €35. €48 and €12.50 are withdrawn and €20 is paid in. What is the balance now?

$35 - 48 - 12.50 + 20 = -5.50$. The balance is −€5.50.

In a number pyramid every brick is the sum of the two bricks below it. At the bottom are $-4$, $x$ and $1$; at the very top is $-1$. What is $x$?

Middle: $-4 + x$ and $x + 1$. Top: $(-4 + x) + (x + 1) = -1$. Trial or working backwards: $x = 1$. Check: middle $-3$ and $2$, top $-1$.

UNIT 24 LESSONS

2Multiplying and dividing

In the pattern $3 \cdot 3 = 9$, $3 \cdot 2 = 6$, $3 \cdot 1 = 3$, $3 \cdot 0 = 0$ the result gets 3 smaller each time. For this to carry on, $3 \cdot (-1)$ must be $-3$. And with $(-3) \cdot \ldots$ the result gets 3 bigger each time: $(-3) \cdot (-1) = 3$.

Dividing is the inverse of multiplying. Because $(-3) \cdot (-4) = 12$, $12 \div (-4)$ must be $-3$. So the same sign rules apply to dividing.

KEY POINT · SIGN RULES

Multiply or divide the absolute values. The sign comes out like this:

Same signs: plus. $\;(-4) \cdot (-5) = 20$, $\;(-20) \div (-4) = 5$

Different signs: minus. $\;(-4) \cdot 5 = -20$, $\;20 \div (-4) = -5$

With several factors: if the number of negative factors is even, the product is positive, otherwise negative. You must not divide by zero.

In everyday life: If the temperature falls by 2 degrees every hour, then 3 hours ago it was $(-3) \cdot (-2) = 6$ degrees warmer.

Brahmagupta wrote as early as the year 628: a debt times a debt gives a fortune. See chapter 2.1.

INTERACTIVE · THE PATTERN CONTINUES
EXAMPLE 3 · FOUR CALCULATIONS

Calculate $(-4) \cdot (-2.5)$, $\;(-12) \div 4$, $\;\left(-\tfrac34\right) \div \tfrac32$ and $\;3 \div (-1.2)$.

$(-4) \cdot (-2.5) = 10$ · $(-12) \div 4 = -3$

$\left(-\tfrac34\right) \div \tfrac32 = -\tfrac34 \cdot \tfrac23 = -\tfrac12$ · $3 \div (-1.2) = -2.5$

EXAMPLE 4 · MANY FACTORS

What sign does $(-2) \cdot 3 \cdot (-1) \cdot (-5) \cdot 4$ have? Calculate the product.

Three negative factors, an odd number: the product is negative. Absolute values: $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 = 120$.

The product is $-120$.

It is 3 °C. For 4 hours the temperature falls by 2.5 degrees per hour. Write the change as a product. How cold is it afterwards?

Change: $4 \cdot (-2.5) = -10$ degrees. $3 + (-10) = -7$. Afterwards it is −7 °C.

Put a number in place of $\square$: a) $(-6) \cdot \square = 42$   b) $\square \div (-4) = 2.5$   c) $(-1) \cdot (-1) \cdot \square = -8$

a) $-7$   b) $-10$   c) $(-1) \cdot (-1) = 1$, so $\square = -8$

Justify without a pattern that $(-1) \cdot (-1) = 1$. Hint: calculate $(-1) \cdot \bigl(1 + (-1)\bigr)$ in two ways.

On the one hand $1 + (-1) = 0$, so the product is $0$. On the other hand, by the distributive law it is $(-1) \cdot 1 + (-1) \cdot (-1) = -1 + (-1) \cdot (-1)$. For this to give $0$, $(-1) \cdot (-1)$ must be $1$.

UNIT 34 LESSONS

3Laws of arithmetic and shortcuts

With $(-25) \cdot 7 \cdot (-4)$ it is best to calculate $(-25) \cdot (-4) = 100$ first and then $100 \cdot 7 = 700$. May you simply change the order? Yes: the laws of arithmetic that you know for natural numbers and fractions also hold for all rational numbers.

KEY POINT · ORDER OF OPERATIONS AND LAWS

Order of operations: brackets first, then powers, then multiplication and division ($\cdot$, $\div$) before addition and subtraction ($+$, $-$), otherwise from left to right.

Commutative law: $a + b = b + a$ and $a \cdot b = b \cdot a$

Associative law: $(a + b) + c = a + (b + c)$ and $(a \cdot b) \cdot c = a \cdot (b \cdot c)$

Distributive law: $a \cdot (b + c) = a \cdot b + a \cdot c$

The commutative and associative laws do not hold for subtraction and division: $5 - 3 \ne 3 - 5$.

Head, paper or calculator? Manageable numbers in your head. A few intermediate steps on paper. Large or awkward numbers with a calculator, but estimate first.

Calculator: You enter the sign with the $(-)$ key, not with the minus key.

EXAMPLE 5 · CALCULATING CLEVERLY

Calculate cleverly: $-3.7 + 5.2 + 3.7$ and $(-8) \cdot \left(-1.25 + 3\right)$.

Swap: $-3.7 + 3.7 + 5.2 = 0 + 5.2 = 5.2$.

Multiply out: $(-8) \cdot (-1.25) + (-8) \cdot 3 = 10 - 24$. $-14$

EXAMPLE 6 · WITH AN ESTIMATE

TRCalculate $(-4.8 + 12.3) \cdot (-2.4)$. Estimate first.

Estimate: $(-5 + 12) \cdot (-2) = 7 \cdot (-2) = -14$.

Exactly: $7.5 \cdot (-2.4)$. $-18$ Sign and size fit the estimate.

UNIT 44 LESSONS

4Powers and square roots

A square has an area of 49 cm². How long is its side? We are looking for a number that gives 49 when multiplied by itself: 7, because $7^2 = 49$. But $(-7)^2 = 49$ too. A side cannot be negative. That is why the square root is defined so that it is never negative.

KEY POINT · POWERS AND SQUARE ROOTS

Power: $a^n = a \cdot a \cdot \ldots \cdot a$ with $n$ factors. $a$ is called the base, $n$ the exponent.

With a negative base: an even exponent gives plus, an odd one minus. $\;(-2)^4 = 16$, $\;(-2)^3 = -8$

Watch the brackets: $(-3)^2 = 9$, but $-3^2 = -(3 \cdot 3) = -9$.

Square root: for $a \ge 0$, $\sqrt{a}$ is the number that is not negative and whose square is $a$. $\;\sqrt{49} = 7$, $\;\sqrt{0.25} = 0.5$, $\;\sqrt{\tfrac{9}{16}} = \tfrac34$. Negative numbers have no square root.

Outlook: $\sqrt{2} = 1.41421356\ldots$ never ends and never repeats. It can be proved that $\sqrt{2}$ is not a fraction. Such numbers are called irrational. You get to know them better in Year 9.

INTERACTIVE · POWERS OF −2
EXAMPLE 7 · POWERS

Calculate $(-3)^4$, $-3^4$ and $\left(-\tfrac12\right)^3$.

$(-3)^4 = 81$ (four negative factors) · $-3^4 = -81$ (the minus is in front of the power)

$\left(-\tfrac12\right)^3 = -\tfrac18$

EXAMPLE 8 · ROOTS

Calculate $\sqrt{1.44}$ and $\sqrt{0.09}$. How long is the side of a square with 2.25 m²?

$\sqrt{1.44} = 1.2$, because $1.2^2 = 1.44$. $\sqrt{0.09} = 0.3$.

$\sqrt{2.25} = 1.5$: the side is 1.5 m long.

Which numbers have the square 36? Which number is $\sqrt{36}$? Explain the difference.

$6$ and $-6$, because $6^2 = (-6)^2 = 36$. But $\sqrt{36} = 6$: the square root is always the number that is not negative.

A square open space has an area of 400 m². How long is one side? How long does it become if the area is four times as big?

$\sqrt{400} = 20$ m. With 1600 m² the side is $\sqrt{1600} = 40$ m, so only twice as long.

Pin down $\sqrt{2}$: show that $1.41 < \sqrt{2} < 1.42$ and find the next decimal place.

$1.41^2 = 1.9881 < 2 < 2.0164 = 1.42^2$. Next: $1.414^2 = 1.999396 < 2 < 2.002225 = 1.415^2$. So $\sqrt{2} = 1.414\ldots$

The lowest temperatures of one week: −3 °C, −1 °C, 2 °C, −4 °C, 1 °C. Calculate the mean.

Sum: $-3 - 1 + 2 - 4 + 1 = -5$. Mean: $-5 \div 5 = -1$. On average −1 °C.

Connecting with chapter 2.1: The distance between two numbers is the absolute value of their difference. Calculate the distance between $-7$ and $4$ and between $-2.5$ and $-6$.

$|-7 - 4| = |-11| = 11$ and $|-2.5 - (-6)| = |3.5| = 3.5$

Is there a rational number that gives $-9$ when multiplied by itself? Justify with the sign rules.

No. A number times itself has two equal signs, so the result is positive or zero, never negative.

EXCURSIONHISTORY

The square root of 2 on a clay tablet

In the collection of Yale University in the USA there is a small round clay tablet with the number YBC 7289. It is probably a practice tablet from a scribal school in Babylonia, almost 4000 years old, from the period between 1800 and 1600 BC. A square with its two diagonals is scratched into it.

On the diagonal, in the base-60 system of the Babylonians, is the number 1; 24, 51, 10. This means $1 + \tfrac{24}{60} + \tfrac{51}{60^2} + \tfrac{10}{60^3} \approx 1.4142130$. The exact value of $\sqrt{2}$ begins with $1.4142136$. So the Babylonians were out only in the seventh decimal place, without any calculator at all.

Sources: Clay tablet YBC 7289, Yale Babylonian Collection, Old Babylonian period. Description: Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative, P255048.

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

PLUS AND MINUS

Subtracting means adding the opposite number: $a - b = a + (-b)$

$-2 - (-7) = 5$

TIMES AND DIVIDED BY

Same signs: plus · different signs: minus

$(-4) \cdot (-5) = 20$, $20 \div (-4) = -5$

LAWS OF ARITHMETIC

Brackets, powers, multiplication before addition · commutative, associative, distributive law

$(-25) \cdot 7 \cdot (-4) = 700$

POWERS

Negative base: even exponent plus, odd minus

$(-3)^2 = 9$, $-3^2 = -9$

SQUARE ROOT

$\sqrt{a} \ge 0$ with $\left(\sqrt{a}\right)^2 = a$, only for $a \ge 0$

$\sqrt{1.44} = 1.2$
